title: When the Oath Sings Revisited
premise: Noor Delacroix, last apprentice of the Vesper Guild, has survived five years of the usurper's anti-magic edicts by selling harmless trinkets and forgetting everything he was taught. When a mute child arrives speaking the First Tongue—the language in which oaths were originally sung—Noor learns the child is a living fragment of the covenant that once bound the mortal realms to their guardian spirits, and that the usurper's armies march to devour what remains. Hunted by oathbreakers and betrayed by the guild's own surviving elder, Noor must gather scattered singers, reforge the broken covenant at the Wellspring, and choose between exposing the truth that will destroy his found family or preserving a lie that will doom the free cities. In the end, he sings the covenant anew with the child's voice joined to his, binding himself as its living anchor—visible at last, at the cost of everything he hid behind.
about_author: Freya Sterling is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval oath rituals before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about people who keep promises in worlds designed to break them.

chapters.title: The Shop That Sold Nothing
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Establishes Noor's quiet life selling inert charms in the occupied city of Corvane, his careful routines, and his deliberate forgetting of guild training. A raid on a neighboring apothecary reminds him how thin his safety is. Emotional beat: the ache of a life built on smallness.

chapters.title: A Knock in the First Tongue
chapters.summary: POV Noor. On a storm night, a child of perhaps eight appears at his door, speaking words Noor hasn't heard since childhood—words that make his old guild-signet glow. The child cannot speak any common language and bears a mark of the Wellspring. Emotional beat: terror and reluctant wonder.

chapters.title: What the Guild Buried
chapters.summary: POV Noor, with flashback interludes. Noor deciphers fragments of the child's speech using his master's hidden primer, learning the child is called Ashen and is a 'living clause' of the old covenant. Emotional beat: grief for the mentor who died keeping secrets.

chapters.title: The Oathbreaker's Warrant
chapters.summary: POV Captain Ilse Varn, hunter of the usurper's Inquisition. She traces rumors of 'singing' in the low quarter and closes in on Noor's street. Her chapters reveal her genuine belief that magic caused the realm's wars. Emotional beat: righteous certainty beginning to crack.

chapters.title: Running Water, Running Names
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Noor smuggles Ashen through the city's aqueducts toward the one person who might help: Sefa, a river-priestess who never renounced her orders. They narrowly evade a checkpoint. Emotional beat: the first taste of chosen risk instead of hiding.

chapters.title: Sefa of the Drowned Bell
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. She recognizes Ashen's mark and reveals the covenant isn't dead—it's starving, kept alive only by scattered singers who no longer know each other. She gives Noor a list of three names and a warning: one of them already serves the usurper. Emotional beat: hope shadowed by distrust.

chapters.title: The Cartographer Who Forgot on Purpose
chapters.summary: POV Noor. First recruit: Brammel, an old guild mapmaker living under a false name, who erased every magical landmark from his own charts to survive. He refuses until Ashen speaks his true name aloud, restoring memories he'd cut away. Emotional beat: the cost of self-erasure.

chapters.title: Ashes Speak
chapters.summary: POV Ashen (rendered in close third with simple, strange cadence). Through the child's eyes we see the world as song and thread; humans are half-silent instruments. Ashen fears being 'closed' like the other clauses were. Emotional beat: loneliness inside a crowd.

chapters.title: Captain Varn's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Ilse Varn. Interrogating a captured singer, she hears the covenant described not as sorcery but as law older than the usurper's crown. Her ledger of executions begins to feel like bookkeeping for a crime. Emotional beat: doubt taking root.

chapters.title: The Third Name
chapters.summary: POV Noor. The trio finds the third singer, Odrik—and discovers he is the traitor, feeding names to the Inquisition in exchange for his daughter's safety. A confrontation ends without blood when Ashen touches Odrik's hands and shows him what he's unmade. Emotional beat: mercy as a harder choice than vengeance.

chapters.title: Odrik's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Odrik. Torn between his daughter held in the usurper's capital and the singers he's betrayed, he offers them passage through the army's supply lines—if they help him steal her back. Emotional beat: loyalty splitting a man down the middle.

chapters.title: Through the Gray Column
chapters.summary: POV Noor. The infiltration of the army camp; Sefa's drowned bell masks their voices from scrying wards. They find Odrik's daughter Mira—but she has been made a small oathbreaker herself, bound to report any singing she hears. Emotional beat: rescue complicated by what captivity makes of people.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Listens
chapters.summary: POV Mira. The girl, nine years old and sharp as glass, has been listening to the usurper's war-councils through her bond. She trades what she knows for freedom: the armies reach the free cities in nineteen days, and the Inquisition seeks the Wellspring itself. Emotional beat: a child choosing which adults to trust.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days
chapters.summary: POV Noor. The company debates: flee beyond the mountains or race the armies to the Wellspring. Noor, for the first time, leads instead of hides, arguing the covenant can't be reforged anywhere else. Emotional beat: claiming a purpose larger than survival.

chapters.title: The Elder Who Survived
chapters.summary: POV Noor. They seek Master Elleryn, the guild's last elder, rumored dead—but she lives, having bought her life by teaching the Inquisition how to detect singers. She justifies it as protecting the guild's future. Emotional beat: betrayal by the person who taught you loyalty.

chapters.title: Truth Against Loyalty
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. Sefa confronts Elleryn while Noor wavers—he owes Elleryn everything. Elleryn reveals the final requirement of reforging: a singer must bind themselves permanently as the covenant's anchor, never again able to hide or lie. Emotional beat: the theme sharpened into a single terrible choice.

chapters.title: Ilse at the Ford
chapters.summary: POV Ilse Varn. Varn's column intercepts the company at a river ford. Instead of fighting, Noor steps forward and lets Ashen sing to her—showing her the memory of the last time the covenant broke, when her own grandmother's village burned unprotected. Emotional beat: an enemy becoming something else.

chapters.title: The Wellspring
chapters.summary: POV Noor. They reach the Wellspring hours ahead of the vanguard, but Elleryn has sold its location too; the Inquisition arrives with siege-mages. Ashen begins the opening verse and falters—one voice alone cannot hold the covenant. Emotional beat: despair at the threshold.

chapters.title: Every Voice We Gathered
chapters.summary: POV rotating: Noor, Sefa, Brammel, Odrik, Mira, even Varn. Each adds a line to the song—not perfect, not trained, but true. The covenant takes root as the armies clash around the spring. Emotional beat: belonging forged in open defiance.

chapters.title: The Anchor
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Climax. To complete the covenant, someone must become its living anchor. Noor accepts, singing his true name into the Wellspring as the usurper's champion breaks through—Ashen's voice joining his, child and man as one clause. The magic floods outward, disarming the armies not with force but with enforced truth: every soldier suddenly hears their own broken promises. Emotional beat: transcendence through sacrifice.

chapters.title: After the Song
chapters.summary: POV Ilse Varn. The usurper's host dissolves as officers confess and desert; Varn lays down her warrant and becomes the first witness for a new order that will try the usurper outside his corrupted courts. She visits Noor, now visibly marked by the covenant, unable to hide anymore. Emotional beat: justice rebuilt from honesty rather than power.

chapters.title: When the Oath Sings
chapters.summary: POV Noor, epilogue. One year later: the guild reopens openly, teaching children—including Ashen and Mira—to sing. Noor can never lie again, and finds the life that costs him nothing to conceal is the first one that feels like his own. Final image: the shop sign repainted to read exactly what it sells. Emotional beat: belonging earned, invisibility surrendered gladly.
